PA3 updated from 3.30.7 to 3.32.4. Here is what changed for you since 3.30.7.

**The bigger changes (3.31 and 3.32)**
- **The journal keeps what we settle.** Claude now files records of our conversations by topic. Each record holds your idea in your words, what I confirmed or corrected, and the outcomes: decisions, findings and parked ideas. Old decisions no longer drop out after a day or two. A fresh Claude starts from the outcomes still in force, and `.claude-state/journal/TOPICS.md` lists every one of them. Filing runs on its own in quiet turns, and the main session shows one quiet `Filed: …` line per topic so you can catch a mistake the same day.
- **The project's past stays findable.** A new index, `docs/PRE_PA3_INDEX.md`, lists the project's older documents. Once per project, one agent also reads the project in the background. It writes a "Living docs" section on the card and a one-page `docs/PRE_PA3_STATE.md` on where things stand. No plan starts until that is done. The card's size limit goes from 7,000 to 10,000 characters.
- **A new `drive` setting.** `autopilot` is the default and works the way tasks always have. `coop` runs nothing while we talk: a batch you lock in runs uninterrupted, then everything stops and I bring you the results.
- **Planners check each plan against every outcome in force.** If a plan contradicts one, the planner names it and says why.

**Fixes (3.30.8 to 3.32.4)**
- **Savings are counted again.** The blue savings figure on the statusline was showing a dash or running low. The first session repairs the ledger once and takes a backup first.
- **Reports no longer go missing.** A finished task no longer waits forever on a helper that has already reported. A report that arrives after a long background build now gets through. A coder's report now always reaches its own expert.
- **Holds and expert launches.** When a hold waits on an update, the reason is now explained. When Claude Code's check gives no verdict on starting an expert, PA3 retries up to three times before stopping the task.
- **Pasted screenshots now reach me.** Before, I only saw "[Image #1]".
- **Statusline.** The Pace, Session, Project and Account lines each have an on/off switch in `~/.claude/usage-ledger/config.json`.
- **New `/pa-bugreport` command.** It writes a file with personal details removed, which you can attach to a GitHub issue.
- **The external-coder reminder now comes once per project** instead of at every session start.

Project Architect 3.32.4, a hotfix (Pictures reach Claude), is installed.

**To load it: /exit, then claude --continue (not /clear)**

We are using DeepSeek. The coder running now isn't cracking functions, it's banking them, and banking is the in-house work we agreed on.

**What we decided.** The card has two lines on this:
- **Cracking.** Every function cracking job goes to DeepSeek and nothing else.
- **Everything else.** Every other coder job stays in-house, and that includes banking.

**What the running coder is doing.** This is bank batch 5. It takes the 7 functions DeepSeek already matched and swaps them into `src/`. Then it updates the tracking tables and runs the full build-and-check gate (the R22 gate). That gate wipes and rebuilds `build/`, so no DeepSeek coder can run at the same time. They'd be compiling against a folder that's being deleted under them.

**What comes next.** Once the bank is committed, the expert starts the cracking queue again on DeepSeek, from batch G18x.

I've released the talk hold, since this doesn't change the plan.

The fix for last time's problem worked, but DeepSeek is back in learning mode for a different reason. This time the friction was real, so I'd leave it alone. G18x is still running, so we don't know yet whether it will come back clean.

**What learning mode is.** PA3 limits a model that's new to the project to one coder at a time. The limit lifts once one of its runs finishes with no friction. Friction means refused or blocked commands, sandbox errors, or a note the expert had to add after the run.

**Last time's problem is fixed.** MiniMax never left learning mode because PA3 counted the judge's approval of each new helper script as friction. Every batch writes new scripts, so no run could ever count as clean. PA3 3.30.4 stopped counting those approvals. Under the new rule, DeepSeek's run G16b came back clean, learning mode lifted, and the expert scaled up to two coders at once, G16x and G18.

**Why it's back.** A model's learning status follows its latest finished run, and G18 hit friction. G16x did too:

| Run | Judge refused | Other friction |
|---|---|---|
| G16x | 1: the command's description said "only checking", but the command also rewrote a score in its results file | 1 whole read of a big file, blocked |
| G18 | 1: a cleanup `rm w*.c` would also have deleted `win.c`, the winning version it had just saved | 1 sandbox failure, re-run |

These aren't false alarms like MiniMax's. In G18 the judge stopped the coder from deleting its own winning code, and in G16x it caught a command doing more than its description said. Counting them as friction is fair.

**Can we exit learning mode now?** There's no switch for it. The only other way would be to edit the run records so a run looks clean, and I won't do that. The way out is a clean run, and G18x, running now, is the next chance. If it finishes clean, DeepSeek gets its 4 lanes back on its own.

**My recommendation.** Leave it as it is. The two slips are different and both are rare, so a note about them probably wouldn't help. Adding a note would also count as friction and keep DeepSeek in learning mode longer. I'll tell you how G18x's run turns out when it finishes.

I've released the talk hold, since none of this changes the plan.
